uncited: Ray-centric rendering computes pixel color by tracing rays from the camera through volumetric data and accumulating density and color along the path, typically executed on the GPU for performance.
The family traces rays from the camera through volumetric data to compute pixel color and opacity.
Rays are marched through the volume using step-based sampling or acceleration structures, with contributions accumulated along the ray path.
It uses a Ray Generation shader, Miss shaders for radiance and shadow, and Hit/Any-Hit/Intersection shaders for volume traversal and shading.

Assign hit group shaders: Closest Hit `__closesthit__volume_radiance` and `__closesthit__volume_shadow`, Any Hit `__anyhit__volume_radiance` and `__anyhit__volume_shadow`, and Intersection `__intersection__volume`.
